java_locations.role: Once a command returns OK_PARTIAL for its opener, feeds subsequent physical lines only to that same command until its own end predicate returns OK or rejects the candidate.
Matches the selected command's starting regex and command-specific end Pattern2; interior lines remain owned while the last line does not match that end pattern.
Defines ordinary floating-note termination as ^[%s]*end[%s]?note$, excluding hnote and rnote terminators.
Uses the same ordinary end-note grammar for ordinary attached notes and a distinct closing-brace predicate for the bracket form.
Intentionally contrasts with ordinary notes by accepting note, hnote, or rnote after end for every sequence note shape.
Expands %s to Java whitespace plus non-breaking space and compiles command patterns case-insensitively, so the optional separator includes a tab.

rust_locations.role: Defines literal ordinary and family-wide terminator helpers, but applies the family-wide helper to every non-brace opener during subtype masking.
Closes buffered non-brace class notes through the literal ordinary helper, which recognizes a regular-space separator but not a tab separator.
Correctly needs the broader sequence-family terminator policy, demonstrating why one global end matcher cannot serve every note command.

claimed_invariant: A multiline note's selected Java command owns its interior until that command's own end predicate matches. Ordinary floating and attached notes close only on case-insensitive endnote or end<one PlantUML whitespace character>note, with optional leading PlantUML whitespace; end hnote and end rnote are ordinary payload. Sequence note, hnote, and rnote commands deliberately share a broader end(note|hnote|rnote) predicate. Final-bracket attached notes close only with their closing brace. Dispatch masking and the eventual consumer must use the same selected-command policy.
causal_divergence: Rust collapsed command-specific end predicates into two string helpers without retaining which command grammar accepted the opener. completed_multiline_note_payload applies is_note_family_terminator to every non-brace opener, so an ordinary class note closes prematurely on end hnote and exposes its remaining payload to subtype scoring. Conversely, is_ordinary_note_terminator recognizes only the two literal strings endnote and end note after trimming, so Java-valid end-tab-note never closes either dispatch masking or the class buffer. The two failures share one causal owner: the missing selected-command terminator policy, not two fixture-specific parser omissions.
planned_model_change: Represent the end policy selected with the opener as an explicit parser value, at minimum OrdinaryEndNote, SequenceNoteFamily, and FinalBracket. Implement one matcher per Java predicate using PlantUML's %s semantics and case-insensitive matching, including zero or one whitespace character between end and note for ordinary commands. Make completed-span discovery retain and use that policy, and make class, sequence, deployment/description, and other consumers call the same policy matcher rather than independently reinterpreting the terminator. Determine policy from the accepted command form and parser context; do not infer it solely from the word note because ordinary and sequence commands overlap. Preserve the rule that incomplete candidates do not mask arbitrary trailing source.
perturbation_axes: ordinary class or DESCRIPTION note versus sequence note, hnote, and rnote command ownership
compact endnote versus one regular space, tab, newline-class whitespace, and non-breaking-space separators
ordinary note bodies containing end hnote or end rnote before the legal ordinary terminator
sequence notes closed by a different sequence note-family terminator
final-bracket attached notes versus ordinary end-note forms
post-terminator declarations or messages versus unterminated trailing source
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns command-specific multiline note end matching and consistent span ownership between dispatch and consumers. It does not own floating-note alias syntax, sequence parallel or vertical-merge prefix semantics, note colors, class SVEK placement, note geometry, subtype score tuning, comparator behavior, baselines, or fixture eligibility.
acceptance: checker_class_wrong_family_text_then_real_end remains CLASS, retains end hnote and all following pre-end-note lines as note payload, and parses the later class command.
checker_class_tab_terminator_post_command parses the colored floating note and the later class with the Java-valid tab separator.
checker_sequence_cross_family_terminator_control continues to close on a different sequence note-family terminator, while the final-bracket control continues to close only on its brace.
Fresh inputs cover at least two whitespace characters, both compact and separated forms, mixed case, a wrong-family ordinary payload line, and an unterminated control.

Parser-level assertions prove dispatch span ownership and consumer construction agree for every tested policy; relevant diff_one --no-oracle perturbations pass except independently accounted rendering residues.
An independent checker attempts to disprove the policy model at the exact implementation revision and records its verdict and all fresh inputs.
forbidden_approaches: using the sequence-family terminator set for every note opener
making end hnote or end rnote special only when a known fixture payload follows
replacing tabs in the whole source or globally normalizing payload whitespace
closing every note-shaped command on a brace
hiding unterminated trailing source to improve subtype scores
fixture aliases, payload keywords, filenames, golden SVG data, score constants, comparator changes, or baseline changes
